title: G2PM: Performance Modeling for ACAP Architecture with Dual-Tiered Graph Representation Learning
problem: Existing performance estimation approaches for Versal ACAP accelerators are either too slow for efficient design iteration or lack accuracy due to the complex AIE array architecture and two-level programming model.
motivation: Accurate and fast performance modeling is critical for enabling efficient optimization and development of accelerators on heterogeneous ACAP platforms.
method: G2PM builds a layered artificial-intelligence model (called a hierarchical graph neural network) that learns about two types of programs used on Versal ACAP chips: kernel programs (individual computation tasks) and dataflow programs (how data flows between tasks). The model organizes this information around the AIE array—the accelerator's main processing engine—to understand both the hardware structure and how software runs on it. This lets the model predict system performance without needing to run expensive full simulations.
key_novelty: Tailoring hierarchical graph representation to both levels of the ACAP's dual programming model (kernel and dataflow) enables accurate performance prediction without simulation.
contributions: G2PM framework: hierarchical graph neural network-based performance modeling for ACAP architecture
Dual-tiered graph representation capturing both kernel and dataflow program characteristics
Achieves <1.6% mean error rate with 4165X speedup over simulation-based methods
primary_theme: ACAP performance modeling with graph neural networks
